description: The `executed` fake credits uact INSTANTLY on the first balance poll after the mint tx (the `tx bme mint-act` branch touches T_MARK at line 30, and the very next `query bank balances` for mode=executed returns uact=16000000 because T_MARK now exists). The real settlement is EPOCH-DELAYED — the script's whole reason for the 30-try poll loop (akt-treasury.sh:64-68) is that uact does NOT rise immediately. Because the fake makes the delta appear on poll #1, a regression that replaced the poll loop with a SINGLE post-mint balance read would still PASS the `executed` case. The test therefore does not prove the poll/epoch-wait behavior is load-bearing. Add an executed variant where uact rises only after N>=2 balance reads (e.g. a counter file) so a no-loop regression FAILS.

evidence.snippet:
*"tx bme mint-act"*)  touch "$T_MARK"; echo '{"code":0}' ;;
... executed) [ -f "$T_MARK" ] && echo '{... uact 16000000 ...}' || echo '{... uact 0 ...}'
